problem: Existing VLM-based exploration judges evidence sufficiency over coarse views or detector-defined objects, and ranks frontiers using semantic relevance or visitation history that only approximate whether the space was actually inspected. This causes early termination or excessive continued search.
motivation: Termination (when to stop) and continuation (where to go) are coupled. A small decisive region in a snapshot, or a target the detector missed, cannot be assessed by whole-view reasoning. Visited is not the same as visually inspected, so nearby frontiers may expose different regions while distant ones overlap in view.
key_idea: Make evidence assessment and frontier evaluation spatially explicit: localize then verify task cues (regions, objects, detector-independent visual points) before terminating, and score frontiers by hidden-space potential minus visual-coverage-based exhaustion and low-progress penalties.
insight: The localize-then-verify evidence probing is the largest contributor: on the A-EQA 41-subset, removing it costs -6.4 LLM-Match and -5.2 SPL. It also cuts average steps from 9.0 to 4.2 while raising the answer score from 3.32 to 3.56, so it is a better stopping rule, not longer search. Frontier regulation mainly helps efficiency: removing visual frontier rejection (VFR) costs 3.9 SPL on A-EQA and 2.1 SPL on GOAT with almost no SR change, and hidden-space scoring helps most in long-horizon goal search. Point-level evidence beats bbox-based localization on the GOAT 278-subset (76.3/50.5 vs 74.2/47.7 SR/SPL).
method: Localization-to-Verification evidence probing: proposes evidence candidates, then navigates toward or crops them and verifies at close range. Only verified candidates can trigger termination.
Answer-oriented probing: splits each snapshot into a 3x3 grid, the VLM picks candidate regions, enlarged crops are verified and answered, and answers are arbitrated for consistency before committing.

Goal-oriented probing: object proposals from object and snapshot memory are locked, approached and verified. Evidential visual points (VLM-predicted pixel in a 3x3 grid cell, back-projected with depth) recover detector-missed targets and are verified at close range.

Cross-temporal frontier association: a quantized position-and-direction key maps transient frontiers to a persistent status memory holding place type and stale count. The stale count resets on decisive evidence and otherwise increments.
Prospective frontier evaluation: U_base = alpha*r + (1-r)^gamma*h, where r is the reactive task-cue score and h the active hidden-space score (AHS), both VLM-derived from the frontier-facing view.

Visual frontier rejection (VFR): a ray-cast visual coverage memory gives the seen ratio of each frontier's mask. Hard rejection requires stale count, coverage, weak stale-adjusted cue and a suppressible place type to all hold.

History-aware low-progress penalty (HLP): a soft penalty on candidates near recent endpoints or the current position, scaled by a low-progress score from displacement-to-path ratio over a window of 4 frontier moves.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) as the default VLM, with YOLO-World, SAM and CLIP for perception; Qwen3-VL/Qwen3.5 variants tested
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (1280x1280, 120° HFOV, camera 1.5 m tilted down 30°) plus pose; TSDF map
setting.action_space: frontier-based waypoint selection with low-level navigation to frontiers or targets

results: ACE reaches 60.4 LLM-Match and 50.2 LLM-Match SPL on A-EQA 184-subset, beating SCOPE (59.1) on LLM-Match and MetaNav (45.5) on SPL. It gets 54.4 SR / 32.8 SPL on HM3D-OVON (vs MetaNav 46.1 SR, BSC-NAV 32.5 SPL) and 69.9 / 76.3 SR on GOAT-Bench full / 278-subset, the best SR among all methods listed. GOAT SPL is below HGR (50.1 full, 56.2 subset).
limitations: Cross-floor navigation is not handled, so the agent may keep searching the current floor.
Instance-level disambiguation of visually similar image-goal targets remains hard, and incomplete annotations cause false negatives.
Heavy reliance on GPT-4o and many VLM calls per step; open VLMs lose accuracy. The HLP effect is not statistically significant (p=0.075, 16 episodes), and many thresholds are hand-set.
